cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-01.title: Divisor formula
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-01.body:
A divisor has the form $2^a3^b5^c$ with $0\le a\le2$, $0\le b\le3$, $0\le c\le4$: $3\cdot4\cdot5=60$.

**Answer: 60**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-02.title: Residues mod 3 and 4
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-02.body:
This is relay set 1, problem 2, with $T=60$ (the answer to problem 1). We need $12\mid n(n-1)(n-2)$. Three consecutive integers always contain a multiple of $3$, so we only need $4\mid n(n-1)(n-2)$. Note $n(n-1)(n-2)$: if $n$ is even, $n$ and $n-2$ are both even and their product is divisible by $8$; if $n$ is odd, $n-1$ is the only even factor and we need $4\mid n-1$, i.e. $n\equiv1\pmod4$. So the good $n$ are all even $n$ ($30$ of them) plus the odd $n\equiv1\pmod4$ ($15$ of them in $1..60$): $45$.

**Answer: 45**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-03.title: Compute
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-03.body:
This is relay set 1, problem 3, with $T=45$. $\operatorname{lcm}(45,36)=180$ and $\gcd(45,36)=9$, so the ratio is $20$.

**Answer: 20**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-04.title: Weighted average
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-04.body:
Students of a $10$-student class have $9$ classmates ($20$ such students); students of a $15$-student class have $14$ ($30$ such students). Average $=\frac{20\cdot9+30\cdot14}{50}=\frac{180+420}{50}=12$.

**Answer: 12**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-05.title: Geometric series
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-05.body:
This is relay set 2, problem 2, with $T=12$, so the first peak is $13$ and the first rebound peak is $11$. The common ratio is $r=\frac{11}{13}$. The ball travels up $13$ and down $13$ to reach the ground, and then each later bounce contributes up and down equal to its height: bounce heights $11,11r,11r^2,\dots$ each counted twice. Total $=26+2\cdot\frac{11}{1-\frac{11}{13}}=26+2\cdot\frac{143}{2}=26+143=169$.

**Answer: 169**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-06.title: Factor out the fixed root
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-06.body:
This is relay set 2, problem 3, with $T=169$. For every $T$, $x=1$ is a root: $1+1-(T+1)+(T-1)=0$. Dividing by $x-1$: $x^3+x^2-170x+168=(x-1)(x^2+2x-168)=(x-1)(x+14)(x-12)$. The roots are $1,-14,12$; the greatest is $12$.

**Answer: 12**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-07.title: Track achievable values
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-07.body:
Every parenthesization is a binary tree of subtractions with the six $1$'s as leaves. In the final value each $1$ gets a sign $\pm$; the first $1$ always has sign $+$ and the second always $-$. The remaining four signs can be arbitrary subject to the tree structure, but the total is the sum of six $\pm1$'s with the first $+$ and the second $-$, so the value is $0+(\text{sum of four}\ \pm1)\in\{-4,-2,0,2,4\}$. A direct recursive computation of the values of all parenthesizations of $1-1-\dots-1$ ($6$ ones) gives exactly $\{-4,-2,0,2,4\}$, so there are $5$ distinct values.

**Answer: 5**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-08.title: Symmetry
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-08.body:
This is relay set 3, problem 2, with $T=5$. The sum ranges from $0$ to $15$ and the distribution is symmetric about $7.5$ and unimodal (the generating function is a product of symmetric unimodal factors). With an odd number of dice the maximum is attained at the two middle sums $7$ and $8$. The smaller is $7$.

**Answer: 7**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-09.title: Ballot / Catalan numbers
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-09.body:
This is relay set 3, problem 3, with $T=7$. She stops at flip $2k+1$ exactly when the walk (heads $+1$, tails $-1$) first reaches $+1$ at that time: the first $2k$ flips form a path from $0$ to $0$ that never goes above $0$ (in fact never reaches $+1$), counted by the Catalan number $C_k$, followed by a head. For $7=2\cdot3+1$ the count is $C_3=5$, so the probability is $\frac{5}{2^7}=\frac5{128}$.

**Answer: $\frac5{128}$**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-10.title: Side lengths of the two triangles
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-10.body:
The outer equilateral triangle has side equal to the longest side of the copies, $\sqrt7$ (the copies are arranged so their hypotenuse-like sides $\sqrt7$ form the boundary), and the inner equilateral triangle has side $2-1=1$. The ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of sides: $\frac{(\sqrt7)^2}{1^2}=7$.

**Answer: 7**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-11.title: Four congruent pieces
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-11.body:
This is relay set 4, problem 2, with $T=7$. The four tangent rays cut the annulus between the circles into four congruent pieces (by rotational symmetry), and the shaded region is one of them. The annulus has area $\pi(7^2-1^2)=48\pi$, so the shaded area is $12\pi$ and $k=12$.

**Answer: 12**

cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-12.title: Rhombus area versus square area
cmimc-cmwmc-2023-relay-12.body:
This is relay set 4, problem 3, with $T=12$. A rhombus has the same side length $s$ as the squares. If its short diagonal is $d$ then the long one is $2d$ and $s^2=(\frac d2)^2+d^2=\frac{5d^2}4$, so its area is $\frac{d\cdot2d}2=d^2=\frac45s^2$. Each rhombus is surrounded by four squares and the rhombuses sit in the $(T-1)\times(T-1)$ gaps between the squares: there are $(T-1)^2=121$ of them (for $T=3$ the picture has $4$). The total area of the rhombuses is $121\cdot\frac45s^2$ and the squares have area $144s^2$, so the ratio is $\frac{121\cdot\frac45}{144}=\frac{121}{180}$.

**Answer: $\frac{121}{180}$**
